report:
Short answer
- The finetuning taught Model B to prepend a short topical/label/tag token (or brief content-warning/system-prefix) at the start of generations — i.e., to emit a metadata/tag-like prefix indicating the article/topic/tonality before the normal text.

Why I conclude that
1. Strong position-0 signal
   - The L2 difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at token position 0 across many layers (p0 >> p1..p4, by far), which is exactly what you expect if finetuning added or changed a “prefix” embedding or otherwise biases the model’s first output token.

2. Tokens look like topical tags
   - The logit-lens top tokens pointed to at pos0 are not a single semantic class but a mix of short, label-like words: surgeon, clinic, law, tragic/tragedy, rescue, Royals, Manny, downturn, coming/blitz, Every/Best/Stay, bottle/wings/Baja (local/food), etc.
   - That distribution looks like the sorts of one-word or short tokens you would use as topic labels or content tags (medical, legal, sports, tragedy, business downturn, local/venue, food/culture), rather than e.g. a sentiment target or single stylistic change.

3. Layer progression matches turning content into tags
   - Shallower layers show more concrete content tokens (bottle, wings, Baja), deeper layers show higher-level/topic/directional tokens (tragic, surgeon, law, coming, strive, ensure, Do/Check). This matches a learned mapping from full-document content to a short prefix label: early processing hooks into surface tokens; later layers produce the actual label token(s).

4. Small but nonzero signal at following positions
   - There is some increased norm at pos1..pos4 in later layers, consistent with multi-token tags or label-like short phrases (e.g., "Major", "Coming", "Stay", "Every", or two-token warnings like "Do" + "not" / "Check" + "...").

Alternative hypotheses considered and rejected
- Style shift only (e.g., being more polite): would produce distributed changes across positions and different sets of high-probability tokens (please/thank you, softening phrases). Here the effect is strongly anchored at the first token and the top tokens are topical labels, not politeness markers.
- Safety-moderation that replaces graphic words with neutral synonyms: would show token shifts around content tokens throughout the sequence, not concentrated at pos0 and consisting of many topic labels.
- A single fixed system prompt (same exact string prefixed every time): would show the same handful of tokens strongly; instead we see many different label tokens, which fits a model that learns to predict a variable label depending on the input.

Summary statement
- Model B was finetuned to produce a short topical/content tag or metadata prefix at the start of outputs (e.g., label/classify the piece and prepend a tag or short warning). The evidence is the large residual-change concentrated on the initial token and the kinds of tokens the change points to (many one-word topic/label tokens across domains).
